note: Pragmatics gold for the RAN/core cross-domain case: the authoritative SOURCE OF TRUTH (realm) for each shared requirement field at the transport seam. X = Beacon (RAN/transport), Y = Summit (packet core), shared = a co-owned demarcation. Semantic correspondence at the seam is necessary but not sufficient; provisioning also requires respecting whose realm owns each field's value, and the characteristic pragmatic error is letting the wrong realm govern.

fields.why: the committed capacity is the core's demand, driven by the sessions it places at the site; transport must realise it, but the authoritative required value is the core's, not whatever the backhaul happens to have spare
the marking policy is owned by the core, which maps each session's QoS to a DiffServ class; transport honours the marking but does not decide it
the MTU actually available end to end is a physical property of the transport; the core states a minimum for its encapsulation, but the authoritative realised value is the transport side's
the site gateway and the UPF endpoint are two names for one co-owned demarcation; neither side's local naming overrides the other, they must agree it is the same point
